extracted.intended_audience: research data managers, repository staff, FAIR implementers, data stewards, funders and policy makers involved in assessing or enabling FAIR data
extracted.subtask_description: Defining and applying metrics and practical tests to evaluate the FAIRness (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability) of research data objects, for use by repositories, researchers, and service providers via manual, semi-automated, or automated tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-F1-01D — Data is assigned a globally unique identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Data is assigned a globally unique identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapped to RDA-F1-02D. No changes to the indicator; assessment details and related resources are specified in the metrics specification. Persistent identifier practice and resolvability are relevant when implementing the metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-F1-02D — Data is assigned a persistent identifier (resolves to digital object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data is assigned a persistent identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from RDA-F1-01D and RDA-A1-03D. The project merged overlapping indicators on persistence and resolvability; PID resolution is considered core functionality. Implementation must handle inconsistencies of PID resolution across providers (e.g., permanent resolution assumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-F2-01M — Metadata includes descriptive core elements to support findability
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata includes descriptive core elements (creator, title, data identifier, publisher, publication date, summary, and keywords) to support data findability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refined from RDA-F2-01M by clarifying a minimum set of metadata properties required to enable data findability and citation, referencing existing guidelines (DataCite, ESIP, IASSIST, EOSC Datasets Minimum Information). Assessment verifies presence of these core metadata descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-F3-01M — Metadata includes the identifier of the data it describes
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata includes the identifier of the data it describes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to RDA-F3-01M. Assessment verifies that metadata carries identifiers that point to the data and data content.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-F4-01M — Metadata is retrievable by machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata is offered in such a way that it can be retrieved by machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rephrased from RDA-F4-01M (originally 'harvested and indexed') to avoid jargon and emphasize automated (machine-aided) retrieval. Assessment details and practical tests specify machine-accessible mechanisms (e.g., metadata endpoints, structured markup).

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-A1-01M — Metadata contains access level and access conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata contains access level and access conditions of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended from RDA-A1-01M to distinguish access condition properties by data types (public, embargoed, restricted, metadata-only). Assessment should verify presence and clarity of access level and legal/administrative access conditions in metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-A2-01M — Metadata remains available even if data no longer available
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata remains available, even if the data is no longer available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from RDA-A2-01M but narrowed in scope to deleted or replaced objects. Practical assessment applies to repository preservation practices: continued access to metadata depends on repository sustainability and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-I1-01M — Metadata uses a formal knowledge representation language
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata is represented using a formal knowledge representation language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligned with RDA-I1-02M. Assessment verifies the use of machine-understandable formal representation (e.g., RDF, JSON-LD) and provides related resources and tests in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-I1-02M — Metadata uses semantic resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata uses semantic resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapped to RDA-I1-01M but distinguishes two types of semantic resources: resources for modelling data (e.g., DCAT) and resources for describing content (e.g., taxonomies). Assessment checks references/use of controlled vocabularies and semantic artefacts where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-I3-01M — Metadata includes links between the data and related entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata includes links between the data and its related entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merged several RDA I3 indicators. Emphasis is on representing links (relations) between data and associated entities (prior version, related datasets, articles, specimens, funder, repository) expressed through relation types and preferably with persistent identifiers for the related entities. Tests verify presence and quality of these links.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-R1-01MD — Metadata specifies the content of the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata specifies the content of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New metric establishing a data content description as essential for assessing data fitness for use. Evaluates whether the dataset's content is specified in the metadata and that the metadata accurately reflects the actual deposited data. Mapped to R1 (data usage license) contextually as content properties are part of plurality of metadata elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-R1.1-01M — Metadata includes license information for reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata includes license information under which data can be reused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines RDA-R1.1-01M and RDA-R1.1-02M. Assessment verifies standard and bespoke licenses; checks for machine-readable license identifiers (e.g., SPDX) and consistency between metadata and license registries.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-R1.2-01M — Metadata includes provenance information
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata includes provenance information about data creation or generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refined from RDA-R1.2-01M by providing minimal metadata properties representing data provenance. Assessment checks for provenance metadata consistent with community standards where available; repositories may need to elaborate properties representing provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-R1.3-01M — Metadata follows community-recommended standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata follows a standard recommended by the target research community of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rephrased from RDA-R1.3-01M to highlight the target research community. Assessment verifies compliance with community metadata standards where applicable; if community standards are lacking, generally applicable standards are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: FsF-R1.3-02D — Data available in community-recommended file format
rubrics_metrics.description: Data is available in a file format recommended by the target research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rephrased from RDA-R1.3-01D and extended to cover both open and future-proof file formats. Assessment checks file formats against community recommendations and considerations for openness and future-proofing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics specification and identifier convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Each metric is specified following a template and identified by a standard naming convention (project short name + FAIR principle identifier + local identifier + whether the metric evaluates data or metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification covers both 'what' (metrics) and 'how' (assessment details). Mapping to CoreTrustSeal requirements is included. The identifier anatomy clarifies metric scope and type; assessment details, resources, constraints and limitations are documented in the specification (see Devaraju et al., 2020a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment modes and use cases (manual, semi-automated, automated)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAIRness of a data object can be assessed manually, semi-automatically, or automatically at different stages across the research lifecycle (e.g., in DMPs, during deposit, or post-publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper presents scenarios and two priority use cases: FAIR-Aware (self-assessment to raise researcher awareness; 10 questions derived from metrics with information tips) and F-UJI (automated assessment for published datasets using PIDs, repository and registry APIs). Implementation recommendations depend on stakeholder motivations, lifecycle stage, and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors influencing assessment scope and outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments depend on context beyond the object and repository (software/services, registries, evaluation approaches, preservation and business management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A functioning FAIR ecosystem requires FAIR-enabling services and trustworthy repositories. Repository certification (e.g., CoreTrustSeal) clarifies capabilities; business information (policies, procedures, workflows) influences object-level FAIRness. Assessments should consider these operational dependencies when interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated testing limitations and scope (human mediation required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated testing depends on clear, machine-assessable criteria; some FAIR aspects (richness, plurality, accuracy, relevance) still require human mediation and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until mechanisms for agreeing community-driven criteria are in place (schemas, usage elements), automated tests must focus on generally applicable data and metadata characteristics. Data quality elements (completeness, correctness, validity, ease of use) are important for reuse but out of scope for these metrics. Assessment specifications must document constraints and limitations transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping and alignment with existing frameworks (RDA, CoreTrustSeal, standards registries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics are mapped to RDA FAIR Data Maturity Model indicators and aligned with CoreTrustSeal requirements and community standards registries (DataCite, re3data, SPDX, RDA Metadata Standards Catalog, LOV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping identifies overlaps and gaps, enabling unification between repository certification and object assessment. Adoption and improvement notes document where indicators were rephrased, merged, or refined based on focus group feedback and practical testing.
